chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whose father, or uncle, or brother provides for his living expenses; is it permissible for him to take from the zakat and thereby expand his means, if they do not provide for him in everything he needs? He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a person receive zakat if their father or brother supports them financially?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between basic subsistence (*ma'unah*) provided by close male kin and the eligibility for zakat to enhance one's standard of living. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that while relatives are obligated to cover essential needs, they are not bound to provide for luxury or improvement, thereby allowing the recipient to utilize zakat funds for such purposes. This distinction highlights the flexibility of zakat distribution in addressing varying degrees of financial need within the family structure.
